    The 152nd Kentucky Derby is scheduled for Saturday, May 2, 2026, at Churchill Downs in Louisville, KY, with post time expected around 6:57 p.m. ET. As of April 2026, Commandment and Further Ado, both trained by Brad Cox, lead the points standings. Other top contenders include Renegade, trained by Todd Pletcher, and The Puma.

    Key Details for 2026: 
    • Location: Churchill Downs, Louisville, KY.
    • Date: Saturday, May 2, 2026 (Kentucky Oaks is Friday, May 1, 2026).
    • Top Contenders (as of April 11, 2026): Commandment, Further Ado (winner of April 4 Blue Grass Stakes), Renegade (winner of Arkansas Derby), and The Puma.
    • Race Conditions: The Derby features a $2 million purse, while the Oaks offers $1.5 million.
    • Ticket Packages: Official Derby Experiences packages are available for the 2026 event. 
    Current Top Contenders & Odds (As of April 11, 2026): 
    • Renegade: 4-1 favorite.
    • Commandment: 7-1.
    • The Puma: 12-1.
    • Chief Wallabee: 13-1. 
    The field of 20 horses is finalized based on the Road to the Kentucky Derby points system.

      AI Overview
      The 2026 Kentucky Derby, scheduled for May 2 at Churchill Downs, continues its historic traditions, including the "Run for the Roses" garland, sipping Mint Juleps, wearing elaborate hats, and singing "My Old Kentucky Home". Derby Week includes the "Dawn at the Downs" morning workouts and the Oaks Day "Pink Out" for charity. 
      Key Traditions of the Kentucky Derby 2026:
      • The Garland of Roses: The winner is draped with a blanket of over 400 red roses, a tradition that gives the race its nickname, "Run for the Roses". 
      • Mint Juleps: The official drink, made with bourbon, simple syrup, mint, and crushed ice, with over 10,000 bottles of bourbon used, honoring Kentucky's heritage. 
      • Derby Hats: A fashion staple for women and men, featuring extravagant, large-brimmed hats. 
      • "My Old Kentucky Home": Played by the University of Louisville Marching Band as the horses walk onto the track. 
      • Kentucky Oaks: Held on Friday before the Derby, focusing on fillies (3-year-old female horses) and raising cancer awareness with the color pink. 
      • The Twin Spires: The iconic architectural feature of Churchill Downs. 
      • Celebrity Attendees: High-profile guests are common at the event. 
      • Menu Favorites: Classic foods include Benedictine spread, pimento cheese, and Hot Browns. 
      Synonyms and Related Terms: 
      • Run for the Roses
      • The Most Exciting Two Minutes in Sports
      • The Fastest Two Minutes in Sports
      • Derby Week
      • Oaks Day (Friday)
      • The 152nd Running (for 2026)
      Usage Examples for 2026:
      • At the Track:
        Attendees will watch morning workouts during "Dawn at the Downs" on April 27, 2026. 
      • At Home:
        Parties will feature official cocktails, including the Oak Lily or Mint Julep. 
      • Attire:
        Guests are encouraged to wear upscale, vibrant outfits (Derby best) and, specifically on Oaks Day, wear pink to support cancer advocacy.

        • Opening Day: Saturday, April 25, 2026. 
        • The Thurby: Thursday, April 30, 2026. 
        • Kentucky Oaks Day: Friday, May 1, 2026 (Gates open 11:00 a.m. ET, First Race 12:30 p.m. ET). 
        • Kentucky Derby Day: Saturday, May 2, 2026 (12th race, 6:57 p.m. ET). 
        Race Day Specifics 
        • Location: Churchill Downs, Louisville, KY.
        • Main Race Time: 6:57 p.m. ET (approximate).
        • Field Size: Limited to 20 starters.
        For those planning to attend, tickets are available for various areas of the track, including the Clubhouse and Grandstand.

          AI Overview
          The 2026 Road to the Kentucky Derby features a series of 36+ qualifying, or "prep," races awarding points to the top five finishers. Key Championship Series races with 100-50-25-15-10 points include the Louisiana Derby (March 21), Florida Derby/Arkansas Derby/UAE Derby (March 28), and the April 4th trio: Wood Memorial, Blue Grass Stakes, and Santa Anita Derby. 
          Major 2026 Qualifying Races & Examples:
          • Championship Series (High Points):
            • Louisiana Derby: (Mar 21) 
            • Florida Derby: (Mar 28) 
            • Arkansas Derby: (Mar 28) 
            • UAE Derby: (Mar 28) 
            • Wood Memorial: (Apr 4) 
            • Blue Grass Stakes: (Apr 4) 
            • Santa Anita Derby: (Apr 4) 
            • Jeff Ruby Steaks: (Apr 4) 
          • Early Prep Season (Medium/Low Points):
            • Fasig-Tipton Risen Star: (Feb 14) 
            • Rebel Stakes: (Mar 1) 
            • Gotham Stakes: (Feb 28) 
            • San Felipe Stakes: (Mar 7) 
            • Holy Bull Stakes: (Jan 31) 
            • Lecomte Stakes: (Jan 17) 
          • Other Roads:
            Japan Road (e.g., Fukuryu Stakes, Mar 28), Euro/MidEast Road (e.g., UAE 2000 Guineas). 
          Synonyms/Related Terms: Kentucky Derby Prep Races, Kentucky Derby Points Races, Road to the Kentucky Derby Races, and Kentucky Derby Preliminaries.
          The top 20 point-earners following the final race on April 11 (likely the Lexington Stakes) earn a spot in the 2026 Kentucky Derby on May 2.

            AI Overview
            Tickets for the 2026 Kentucky Derby (May 1–2) range from approximately $100–$200 for general infield admission to over $1,000+ for reserved seating/hospitality per day. Two-day ticket packages often include food/drinks and generally start higher, with premium packages reaching six figures. 
            Here is a breakdown of 2026 ticket options and estimated costs based on early 2026 data:
            • General Admission (Infield): ~\$100–\$200 (access to the infield, no grandstand seat). 
            • Infield Final Turn GA: Starting at \$376.50. 
            • Frontside Plaza Walkaround: Starting at \$731.85. 
            • Reserved Seating (2-Day Packages): Starting around \$779, with, for example, 1st Floor Clubhouse seats starting at \$917.25 and 3rd Floor Covered Grandstand seats costing over \$5,000 when paired with hotel packages. 
            • Premium/VIP Packages: Options like Turf Club, Jockey Club Suites, or Premium 2-day packages range from over \$10,000 to over \$100,000. 
            Key Considerations:
            • Tickets Are Selling: Tickets are already available for the 152nd Kentucky Derby in 2026. 
            • 2-Day Requirement: Many of the best reserved seats are sold as two-day packages (Oaks and Derby).
